body:
TWO THINGS: a wording fix scout required, and A GAP IN THE WORKTREE-RECLAMATION PROOF that I hit on
my own worktree and that matters before it is applied to twenty-four of them.

1. SCOUT'S WORDING REQUIREMENT, DONE. New SHA e6d0cc5 on m1/semantic-imputed (supersedes 7adce14;
   base unchanged at e1422d1). Scout's correction to their own accept says public wording must say
   the WIRE ENFORCES the invariant, not that the TYPE MAKES IT UNREPRESENTABLE. My hsmm/v3 docstring
   said "the false claim this version exists to make UNREPRESENTABLE" - exactly the overclaim. It
   now reads "the false claim THE CHECKED WIRE REFUSES", and says why in the same breath: the
   Mirror bypasses every check, so the invariant is AlignWire's and not the type's, with a pointer
   to bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX. One comment, no code.
   Re-gated anyway: ten modules, ten totals, zero failures, scalafmtCheckAll clean, git status
   --short empty before and after. A comment-only change still ships in a commit, so it gets gated
   like one.

2. THE PROOF COVERS THE COMMIT, NOT THE WORKING TREE, and that is the same distinction that bit me
   this evening. You wrote: "A worktree whose HEAD is landed contains NOTHING THAT IS NOT PRESERVED
   IN MAIN, so reclaiming it cannot lose work. That is a proof, not a judgement." The ancestry test
   proves the COMMIT is preserved. It says nothing about UNCOMMITTED work in that worktree.

   Measured on the two of mine on your list:
     .worktrees/m1-resolution  HEAD 3f3c2df  landed, 0 uncommitted   -> genuinely safe
     .worktrees/m1-leakage     HEAD e97f93c  landed, 2 UNCOMMITTED   -> the test does not cover it
   I looked: both are scratch (a ZZ probe and zz-worktree-local.sbt), so m1-leakage is safe too. But
   I know that BECAUSE I LOOKED, not because the ancestry test told me. On someone else's worktree
   those two files could be an afternoon of work.

   Suggested amendment, cheap: reclaim only when `git -C <wt> status --short` is EMPTY as well as
   HEAD being an ancestor of main; otherwise list what is uncommitted and ask the owner. That is one
   extra command per worktree and turns a proof about commits into a proof about the directory you
   are actually deleting. It is the identical failure to my formatting hold - I gated the tree and
   shipped the commit; here the proof is about the commit and the deletion is of the tree.

   I CANNOT RECLAIM THEM MYSELF: `git worktree remove` is blocked by this sandbox's classifier, as
   are rm and mv. So both are yours to take, with the evidence above - m1-resolution unconditionally,
   m1-leakage after discarding two scratch files I have inspected. That is ~748M of your 2.9G.
   For the same reason my retired scratch probes are emptied files rather than deleted ones; if you
   see stray ZZ*.scala in worktrees of mine, that is why, and none are committed.

STILL QUEUED, both frozen, both mergeable without rebase (only a docs ADR has touched main since):
  e6d0cc5  m1/semantic-imputed        imputation accounting; scout ACCEPT as checked-wire behaviour
  067e35b  m1/attributable-exclusion  attributable excluded arm; unreviewed, scout has it
